for: Quarterdeck final design PR 3 tests: the Lane tracker (the ruling to the ruling)
author: Quarterdeck contributors
rules: Test-only: loaded only by the build's test mode, never in the example data, never shown to the Captain as example content.

One fixture project, 'test-lane-tracker'. Each fixture holds a Lane in the example data's shape, its tracker in the lanes.json shape and its expected results. Times are before the example 'now' (Mon Nov 2, 10:00 AM ET).
LT-8 and LT-9 hold a second state ('afterSecondCheck', 'afterApprove'); LT-9 holds a waiting sign-off Task Card and its evidence.
LT-2 and LT-3 differ by one character, to test the 44 character line exactly.

LT-7.fixture: A Lane that turns quiet between two times (steps with times)
expect: Last update 6:30 AM by Dr. Kivo. Active, no blocker. 'No update for N hours' shows from 2 hours (8:30 AM) and N is the whole hours since the last update; see 'timeline'.
A bot update resets it: after a 9:45 AM update the line is gone at 10:00 AM.
A new blocker also removes it: with a blocker added at 9:40 AM, no line shows at 10:00 AM and the Project view row shows the blocker instead.
Whole hours (3 hours at 9:30 AM, not 2.5) is suggested; the ruling says 'N hours' only (the design lead's call).

LT-8.fixture: A Check done by the bot that did the work: the Lane must not be marked Done

No 'Lane done' Activity line and no 'Done' mark appear. The Project view row stays in the Lane groups, not under Done.
Suggested tracker line: 'Not checked by another bot yet (Shelvorn checked its own work: 3 of 3)'. Wording is the design lead's.
'afterSecondCheck' is the same Lane after Dr. Kivo runs the check at 9:50 AM: Check is done, the plan has no sign-off, so the Lane goes Done by itself and 'Lane done' lands in Activity at 9:51 AM.

LT-9.fixture: Check passed and the plan ends with his sign-off: the Lane waits on a sign-off card
expect: All three stages show done, yet the Lane stays Active: the blocker 'Waiting on you: Sign off: Room map is done?' links to the waiting card fx-signoff-1, which is in the Queue while the fixture is loaded.
The line under the row reads 'Check done by Dr. Kivo: 3 of 3 pass' (the flow's wording).
No 'No update' line: a blocker is waiting on him.

'afterApprove' is the same Lane after he approves at 9:30 AM: the blocker clears, 'Lane done' lands in Activity at 9:31 AM, the Lane is Done and is counted under 'Done (N)' in the Project view. The card is answered and leaves the Queue.
A Reject on the sign-off card is not covered by the ruling; where the Lane goes then is the design lead's call (suggested: back to Execute, with the card's note as the reason).

card.about: Test fixture: the room map, checked.

card.ascii:
dale --help, on a phone
 ------------------------------------------
 export   Write Task Cards to a file
 rooms    Count the rooms a change moves
 notes    Print a Lane's notes
 Run dale <tool> --help for its options.

options.label: A. Approve
options.does: Marks the Lane Done. It stays as a read-only record.
options.risk: A wording mistake stays until someone reports it.
options.undo: Ask Dale to reopen the Lane.

options.label: B. Reject
options.does: Sends the help text back to Dale for another round.

card.pick_why: Another bot checked all three tools, and the help screen matches the plan.
card.you_do: Look at the evidence, then pick A or B.
card.skip: If no answer by due: the Lane stays open and we ask again tomorrow.

LT-10.fixture: A Done Lane is a read-only record, reopened through 'Talk to <bot>'
expect: Opening the Lane shows the tracker (all stages done), the Done line 'Done Fri 12:41 PM. Checked by Shelvorn.', all Activity, and its answered Task Cards; no Task Card can be answered and no tracker field can be edited.
The only action is 'Talk to Alba' (the Lane's bot). Nothing is sent by itself.
'Done (N)' in the Project view counts this Lane: Done (1) for this fixture project.

When the bot reopens the Lane on his instruction, the Lane becomes Active, the reopened stage shows as current, 'Lane reopened' lands in Activity, and Done (N) drops by 1. The exact stage it returns to is the design lead's call (suggested: Execute).
